How the dispatch app works

What each screen is for, what to press, and what drivers, site heads and customers get on their phones. Keep this open the first few weeks.

Start hereWho sees what

In shortOffice logins get the reception screen. Dispatchers get the Board and can text drivers. Admins also get Setup.

Everyone logs in at dispatch.joshtemp.site (later dispatch.adamsbros.ca). What you see depends on your login.

Office / receptionOffice login

The reception screen: take a call, price it, book it, find a customer, answer questions, and the Our sites page. Can make work orders but can't text drivers.

DispatcherDispatcher login

The Board: everything office can do, plus assign drivers, text them, mark jobs done, read drivers' texts and the Records tab.

Admin / ownerAdmin login

Everything, plus Setup: drivers, trucks, logins, prices, work order fields, site heads, equipment, texting times and backups.

Overnight snow dispatcher login. Sees only the ❄ Snow call page: start a call-out, watch who's coming, and keep the shovelers list. Nothing else in the app.

The routineA day with the app

In shortCalls get booked all day. At 3:30 PM site heads are asked what they need. The office hands it out and confirms. At 6:30 AM drivers get their day. They reply OK, then DONE.

Times are the usual settings. An admin can change them under Setup.

  1. All dayReception

    Customer calls are priced and booked on the reception screen. Website orders land in Website requests on the Board, ready to schedule.

  2. 3:30 PMAutomatic

    Every active site head gets a text asking what they need for the next work day. On Friday it asks about Monday.

  3. AfternoonSite heads

    They reply in plain words ("tandem AM, mini ex, 2 labourers"), tap the link, or call in. Replies show on the Our sites page.

  4. Before closeOffice

    On Our sites, give each site its trucks and drivers, machines and labourers, then that's saved as you go. Machines that need moving get their float work order made automatically. Press Tell site heads what's coming so each one knows.

  5. 6:30 AMAutomatic

    Each driver and labourer gets one text with that day's jobs: where, what, their own load, and a link to the job page. Drivers are only told the morning of.

  6. During the jobDrivers

    They reply OK to confirm, tap +1 load on the job page, text a photo of the scale ticket, and reply DONE when finished. The Board updates as they go.

  7. After the jobAutomatic, if on

    An hour after every driver is done, the customer can get a text asking for a Google review (once a year at most, 9 AM to 8 PM).

DispatchersThe Board

In shortEach card is a work order. Cards move from To text to Waiting for OK to Working to Done as drivers reply. The yellow button is the next step.

One day at a time. Every work order is a card, sorted into lanes by where it's at.

Date bar
‹ Today › and the date picker move between days. Lanes / List / Map / Calendar change the view.
Tiles
Active, Needs attention (not texted, no reply, a problem), Done today, Drivers free, and Website requests waiting to be scheduled. Click one to filter.
Type chips
Show one kind of work order. 🏗️ Our site shows only work for our own job sites.
Drivers row
Each driver's jobs for the day and whether they've been texted.
Lanes
To text → Waiting for OK → Working → Done. A card moves along by itself as drivers reply.
Text drivers their day
Sends every driver their list for the day on screen now, if you don't want to wait for the morning text.

Reading a card

  • Top line: work order number, time (First thing / AM / PM / Any time) and type. Work for our own sites says OUR SITE, floats moving our machines too.
  • Middle: what it is, where from and to, customer or site contact.
  • Driver line: each driver, their truck, and their status: Not texted Texted – waiting Confirmed ✓ Working Done ✓. Needs update means the job changed after they were texted.
  • Big button: the one thing to do next, e.g. Text 1 driver, Re-send text, Mark complete.
  • More: print, copy to another day, history, book pick-up (bins and toilets), cancel or delete.

EveryoneMaking a work order

In short+ New job, pick the type, fill in when, who and where, tick the drivers, Save. Saving never texts anyone.

  1. Press + New job (or New call on reception) and pick the type: Aggregate, Bin, Septic, Toilet, Float, Labour, Our site or Misc. The form changes to match the paper form for that type.
  2. Fill in the date and time (First thing, AM, PM or Any time), the customer and the address. Start typing a name to pick a past customer.
  3. Prices fill in from the price book as you go. Drivers never see prices.
  4. Dispatchers tick the drivers and pick each one's truck.
  5. Save work order. If something required is missing, the form says what. Booking far ahead with details to come? Use Save as draft: drafts can't be texted until finished.
Saving never texts anyone. Drivers get it in the morning jobs text, or when a dispatcher presses the button on the card.

Office & dispatchOur sites

In shortPick a site, read what the site head asked for, and add trucks, machines and labourers. It saves as you go. Then tell the site heads what's coming. Floats for machines are made for you.

For our own jobs: the trucks, drivers, machines and labourers each site head needs. This replaces the end-of-day phone calls and the paper sheet. Open it from the Our sites tab on the Board, or 🏗️ Our sites on reception.

The three steps

  1. Ask. Site heads are texted "what do you need?" by themselves at 3:30 PM on work days. The count shows how many replied. Ask the 2 who haven't replied sends it again to just those.
  2. Hand out. Give each site what it needs (below). A site counts as ready once it's been given something, or said it needs nothing.
  3. Confirm. Tell site heads what's coming texts every ready site head their list. Drivers are not texted until the morning.

Working through a site

Click a site on the left. Its chip says where it stands: No reply yet, Replied, Ready, Told or Nothing needed.

  1. They asked for. Their words as sent, how they replied, and below them the app's reading. Took it on the phone? Type it in the box and press Add.
  2. Already on site. Machines sitting at that site, since when. Done with one? Back to the yard makes the float work order to bring it home.
  3. Add what they need with + Truck, + Machine and + Labourer. Each opens a list with what's free on top; anything busy is greyed out with the reason, e.g. "customer: Smith". Picking a driver fills in their usual truck. For a truck, fill in what it's hauling and how many loads. Click a truck in the list to change it, or × to take anything off.
  4. Machines. The list says where each machine is. If it isn't at the site yet, adding it makes its float work order, from wherever it is. It shows on the Board as an OUR SITE float: give it a float truck and driver there.
  5. Note for the site head, e.g. "float arrives 7:30".
  6. Everything saves as you go ("Saved ✓"). Press Tell Mike what's coming to text just this site head, or use step 3 for all of them. Change something after they were told and the site goes back to Ready, so you can tell them again.
Also on the page. What's free at the bottom opens a list of free trucks, drivers and machines in the yard. Ask Mike again re-asks one site head. The ‹ › arrows look at other days, e.g. Friday planning for Monday. Print gives one sheet with every site. On a phone, you see the list first; tap a site to open it.

On their phonesWhat people get by text

In shortSite heads get asked in the afternoon and confirmed before close. Drivers get one text the morning of, with only their own load.

Site head · 3:30 PM
Hi Mike - what do you need at Seguin on Mon Nov 16? Reply e.g. "tandem AM, mini ex, 2 labourers", or "same", or "nothing". Or tap: dispatch…/s/…
tandem of A gravel AM, 4 loads, mini ex and 2 labourers
Thanks Mike - got it for Seguin on Mon Nov 16: Tandem (AM) – A Gravel 3/4", 4 loads, Mini excavator, 2 labourers. We'll text you what's confirmed.
Site head · confirmation
Hi Mike - for Seguin on Mon Nov 16 you have: T4 with Dave Thompson (A Gravel 3/4", 4 loads), Mini excavator 1 (floated from the yard), Sam Lee. Note: float arrives 7:30
Driver · 6:30 AM
Your job for Mon Nov 16: Adams Bros - Our Job Site #1011 Mon Nov 16 AM Truck: T4 Your load: A Gravel 3/4", 4 loads Site address: 12 Lake Rd, Seguin Site contact: Mike Rivers 705-555-0200 Reply OK to confirm. Reply DONE when finished. Details: dispatch…/j/…
OK

Drivers only see their own load, never prices or the site's machine list. The job page behind the link has the map, the +1 load and Finished buttons, and a button to add a ticket photo.

Dispatch & adminsBoard tools

In shortThree buttons along the top of the Board: plan the shortest route, see what repeats, and read or text the day's summary. Admins can invoice a finished job from its More menu.

🗺 Plan route

  1. Pick the day, a driver (or everyone), and the kind of work order. Septic is ticked to start.
  2. The app puts the stops in the shortest loop from the yard and back. Customers' times come first: First thing, then AM, then PM, then Any time.
  3. Check the order, the km and the drive time. Shorter by says how much it saves over the Board's order.
  4. Save this order: the Board and the drivers' morning text follow it. Nobody is texted and no times change. Open in Google Maps shows the route.

A stop the map can't find is listed underneath: open the work order and fix the address, or drop a pin.

🔁 Repeating work orders

  1. On a work order, set Repeat: every 1 to 4 weeks on the days you tick, or every 1 to 3 months on the same date. Choose when it ends: never, on a date, or after a number of visits.
  2. Visits appear on the Board two weeks ahead, marked 🔁, with no driver. Pick the driver for each one as usual.
  3. Changing a visit asks: This visit only, or This and future visits (the new details, and a new repeat if you change it, from that visit on).
  4. The 🔁 Repeating button lists them all: skip one date, pause, or stop repeating (e.g. when a rental toilet is picked up).

Day summary

Press Day summary for the day on the Board: jobs done, loads hauled, the work done in dollars (before HST), what was booked today, every job still open and why (no driver, not texted, no OK yet), website orders, machines moved, and tomorrow.

Tick the numbers to send it to (saved in Setup) or type another, then Text it. It can also go out by itself every day (Setup → Alerts & day summary).

Invoices (admins)

On a priced work order, More → Send invoice to QuickBooks… makes the invoice in QuickBooks from the work order's prices, closes its estimate, and can email it to the customer. The invoice number goes on the work order. It needs QuickBooks connected, and every line priced.

Winter · overnight❄ Snow call

In shortOne button phones every shoveler. Each one is called at their own call-ahead time, hears the start time and place, and presses 1 if they're coming or 2 if they can't. The screen fills in as they answer.

Starting a call-out

  1. When do they start? Tap a time (or Other), then Today or Tomorrow. After midnight, "Today" is the morning you're in.
  2. Where? The yard is filled in. Add a note if needed, e.g. "Downtown route first".
  3. Who? Everyone is ticked. Untick anyone who's off. Each card says when they'll be called (their call-ahead time before the start).
  4. Check the line at the bottom: Start and First call. A warning shows if the time has passed or is more than 20 hours away (wrong day).
  5. Press Start snow call, then press it again to confirm.

Call everyone right now skips the call-ahead times. Text me the results texts the numbers you tick as people answer.

Watching who's coming

  • Coming / Waiting / Can't: everyone moves across as they answer. The big number is how many are coming.
  • They answer by pressing 1 or 2 on the call, or by texting 1 or 2 back.
  • No answer? They're called again 5 minutes later, up to 3 calls, then listed under Can't / no answer.
  • Call now rings that person straight away. Coming / Can't marks them yourself, e.g. if they phoned you.
  • Cancel the call-out stops it; anyone already coming is told.
  • When it's over the results stay on screen. Clear the board takes them off (they stay in the records).

Shovelers and the setup text

Shovelers are their own list (not drivers). Each has a name, cell and call-ahead time: how long before the start they need the call. Add, edit or switch someone off with Edit.

Phones often silence or flag calls from numbers that aren't saved, so every shoveler gets the setup text once. They reply SNOW, then get our number to save and how to make it a Favourite. The list shows who has replied.

Shoveler · setup text
Hi Mike, it's Adams Bros. This winter our snow call-outs will phone you from 705-…, usually early in the morning. Please reply SNOW so we know you got this, and we will send you the contact to save.
SNOW
Thanks Mike! Save our number 705-… as "Adams Bros Snow Call" (or open the link to add it). Then make it a Favourite so the call rings through Do Not Disturb at night.

The call voice (dispatchers and admins)

Calls use the phone system's voice unless an ElevenLabs voice is set up. To use one: add ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in Replit's Secrets and Republish, open Call voice at the bottom of the Snow call page, Choose a voice (▶ Hear our call plays a sample), then press Record the usual lines now. The greeting, start times from 3:00 to 8:00 AM, the yard and "Press 1…" are recorded once and kept; calls then play them for free and the key can be removed. A new place or note is read by the phone system's voice unless the key is still there.

Office loginsReception screen

In shortNew call to price and book. Find to change or cancel. Customer asks for prices and answers. Our sites for site heads calling in.

New call
Pick the service, answer a few questions, and the price works itself out. Then who, which day, and book it, or save it as a quote to call back.
Find
Search by name, phone, address or W.O. # to change or cancel a booking. A texted driver is told if their job is cancelled.
Customer asks…
Prices and the standard answers to common questions.
Our sites
The same page the dispatcher uses, so reception can take site heads' calls and fill in what they need.

Notes from the boss show on the home screen when posted.

AdminsSetup

In shortPeople, trucks, logins, text times, work order fields, sites, equipment and backups. Changes take effect right away.

Set once, change any time. Only admins see this tab. Pick a section in the menu on the left (a dropdown on phones); Overview shows how everything is set up, and anything that needs a look is shaded yellow. Lists open an item in a side panel to edit it.

  • Drivers, labourers & trucksNames, cell numbers and each driver's usual truck.
  • LoginsWho can log in, and as office, dispatcher, admin or overnight snow dispatcher (Snow call only). The owner manages these.
  • Our sitesSite heads (name, cell), sites (name, address, who runs it, Active) and equipment (name, kind, unit #, where it is now, in the shop). Tick the box to text site heads automatically at 3:30 PM.
  • Drivers' jobs textSet to for today, the morning of, at 6:30 AM so drivers hear about their day that morning.
  • Work order fieldsRename, hide, reorder or add the boxes on each type of work order.
  • Required fieldsWhat must be filled in before a work order saves.
  • Review requestsPaste the Google review link and switch on the after-job review text.
  • Alerts & day summaryThe cell numbers that get a text when something goes wrong (texts not sending, a backup failing, the app having been down), and who gets the day summary, and when. Send a test alert to check.
  • BackupsCopies every hour (when something changed) and every night. Google Drive gets the nightly copy too, once connected. The owner can restore everything, or only Our sites.

EveryoneOther tabs

In shortCustomers, Prices, Questions and Records: look things up, keep the price book and answers current, and pull old work orders.

Customers
Everyone we've done work for, built up from work orders. Search by name, phone or address, open a customer to see their past work orders, and see who's due for a septic pump-out.
Prices
The price book the app prices work orders from: aggregates, delivery by distance, septic, bins, toilets and water. Admins change prices here; every change is logged, and work orders keep the price they were booked at.
Questions
Standard answers to what customers ask, so everyone gives the same answer. Reception sees them under Customer asks.
Records
Dispatchers: find work orders by date range, status, type or name; print a batch; or download a spreadsheet, e.g. for tax time.

When something looks offGood to know

In shortMost problems are a driver not texted yet, a machine recorded in the wrong place, or a site head who hasn't replied.

Nobody was called for the snow call.

Check the day: the line above the Start button says when the first call goes out. A call-out set for Tomorrow by mistake waits until tomorrow. Cancel it and start again with Today, or use Call now on each person.

A shoveler says the snow call showed up as spam, or didn't ring.

Ask them to open the setup text (it may be in their spam or "Unknown senders" folder), mark it Not spam, reply SNOW, save the number and make it a Favourite. Use Send to everyone again under Shovelers if they can't find it.

I got an "ADAMS BROS DISPATCH ALERT" text.

It says what went wrong. Texts not sending: check the texting number in Setup and tell whoever handles the texting account. Backup failed: press Back up now in Setup → Backups; if it fails again, call for help. App was down: texts that came in while it was down were missed, so check with drivers and site heads. The same kind of alert comes at most once an hour, and Setup → Alerts lists them all.

The app was off for a few minutes after an update.

Normal: a Republish takes the app off for about 10 minutes. Do updates after hours. Planned updates don't send an alert.

A repeat visit is on the wrong day, or shouldn't happen.

Open 🔁 Repeating and skip that date (it won't come back), or open the visit and change This visit only.

A driver says they didn't get their job.

Check their line on the card. Not texted means it hasn't gone yet: press the big button on the card. Needs update means the job changed: press Re-send text. Check their cell number under Setup.

A site head didn't reply.

Their card says no reply yet. Tap their number to call, or Text Mike to ask again. Type what they say into the box on the card.

How does the app know where a machine is?

From what's been done in the app: the last site it was given to, the last float that moved it, or the last time it was sent back to the yard. A new machine starts in the yard. When you start out, an admin sets each machine's real spot under Setup → Our sites → Equipment → Where it is now (no float is made).

A machine shows at the wrong site.

It was moved without the app. An admin fixes it under Setup → Our sites → Equipment → Where it is now: that changes it straight away and makes no float.

I gave a site a machine by mistake.

Remove it on the card and Save. Its float work order is removed too, as long as no driver has been texted about it.

A job finished early or was called off.

Dispatchers: More → Mark complete, or More → Cancel job. Drivers who were texted are told when a job is cancelled.

Where did a text from a driver go?

Texts the app understood (OK, DONE, photos) go on the job. Anything else is flagged under All texts from drivers on the Board.
